body.statement: The allocation-tube theorem and its matching primal construction imply \[R_n(c^\dagger)=n^{-1}-\mathfrak L^\dagger n^{-4/3}+o(n^{-4/3}),\qquad 0<\mathfrak L^\dagger<\infty.\] The lower bound holds against every outcome-independent dependent assignment law and every randomized labeled-data estimator, and the upper bound is attained by total finite procedures. Thus existence of the all-design limit at \(c^\dagger\) is a consequence of the proved tube theorem rather than the proposal's root assertion.
body.justification: This short consequence converts the local orbit saddle into the sharp unrestricted decision value at the designated unequal contrast.
body.gap: The accepted parent's rate and subsequential certificate results do not imply convergence or identify a constant at \(c^\dagger\).
body.consumer: It gives a sharp worst-case precision benchmark for a fixed-horizon three-regimen trial using the \(1:-1/4:-3/4\) contrast.

obligation.what_is_open: A matching all-design second-order converse and primal upper expansion identifying a common constant \(\mathfrak L^\dagger\), including proof that this constant is finite and positive.
obligation.obstruction: The asserted implication depends on the unresolved allocation-tube expansion. The exact finite Bayes inequality alone gives no asymptotic coefficient, while the attaining-side construction gives only the opposite one-sided bound. The frozen dependencies also contain no proved quantitative statement that a coefficient saddle yields the claimed finite procedures.
obligation.attempted: The independent-design Airy procedure was proved to give the positive lower limit for the minimax deficit, and the tube prior was transferred exactly to every dependent design through allocation counts. Without a uniform expansion of the fixed-count Bayes risks, these two bounds cannot be matched.
obligation.partial_result:
The attaining-side theorem and \(\kappa(c^\dagger)=5/8\) prove
\[
\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{4/3}\{n^{-1}-R_n(c^\dagger)\}
\ge C_A(5/8)^{2/3}>0.
\]
The orbit lemma supplies a valid finite Bayes lower bound for every design, but no proved expansion of that bound identifies its limit or matches the attaining coefficient.
